dhpak2.4:1.1: The English story title follows the local Pāli title. The alternate romanized title Bālanakkhattaghuṭṭhavatthu and editorial heading ‘A Festival of Fools’ were removed because they have no separate Pāli passage.
dhpak2.4:2.1: The opening quotation represents Pamādamanuyuñjantīti (‘They cultivate heedlessness’), not the later words ‘Foolish, stupid people.’
dhpak2.4:3.1: bālanakkhattaṃ nāma saṅghuṭṭhaṃ says the festival was proclaimed in Sāvatthī; the earlier English said it was celebrated there.
dhpak2.4:3.4: lajjantā nāma natthi and koci kassaci na lajjati concern absence of shame before others, not absence of respect. pabbajitaṃ includes renunciants, not only bhikkhus.
dhpak2.4:3.5: Dvāre dvāre ṭhatvā asabbhaṃ bhaṇanti says they stood at doorways uttering coarse speech; it does not say they specifically insulted people they met.
dhpak2.4:3.7: aḍḍhaṃ vā pādaṃ vā kahāpaṇaṃ vā means a half, a quarter, or a whole kahāpaṇa according to means; the English had called the last payment a penny.
dhpak2.4:5.1: buddhappamukhaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ specifies the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by the Buddha.
dhpak2.4:5.3: atidukkhena describes the disciples' seven days as a time of great distress, rather than merely unpleasant.
dhpak2.4:7.1: The repeated Pāli transcription of verse 26 and editorial section label were removed because they have no separate local Pāli passage.
dhpak2.4:8.1: mā kāmaratisanthavaṃ, explained as vatthukāmakilesakāmesu ratisaṅkhātaṃ taṇhāsanthavaṃ, warns against attachment to sensual pleasures; the former English reduced this to ‘do not take delight in pleasure.’ The repeated Pāli transcription of verse 27 was removed.
dhpak2.4:9.1: The extensive Pāli explanation of verses 26 and 27 has no English translation and remains Pāli-only under this paragraph.
dhpak2.4:10.1: Mahājanassa sātthikā dhammadesanā jātā says the Dhamma teaching was beneficial to many people; the English had recast this as a separate benefit that arose from the teaching.
dhpak2.4:11.1: The Pāli closing title Bālanakkhattasaṅghuṭṭhavatthu catutthaṃ is Pāli-only; it has no English key.
